integrity: The day-resolved 1979 Holmes source was checked for the exact forced double-well equation and strange-attractor scope. The 1980 Holmes record was checked for forced-oscillation scope and primary dynamical-systems classification. A complete open 2017 same-family article was inspected through its equation, Melnikov analysis, Lyapunov-exponent discussion, and bifurcation results; targeted full-text searches found no mean-square, average, variance, or conditional formulation. The 1982 statistical Duffing abstract was checked specifically because it discusses time and ensemble averages and is retained as a residual literature risk rather than being treated as full-text noncoverage. Published semantic searches covered invariant measures, stationary power, conditional regressions, RMS velocity, well-minimum crossings, and variance defects. The conditional laws, strict equality obstruction, quadrature response, load variance defect, and one-well crossing theorem were independently reconstructed and replayed with the packaged exact checker.
scientific_limitations: The theorem assumes harmonic forcing with nonzero frequency and positive double-well parameters.
It is stated for compactly supported invariant probability measures.
The strict RMS velocity ceiling is not claimed to be an attained sharp maximum.
The mechanical input-dissipation identity is prior structure and is not claimed as original.
The 1982 statistical Duffing source was compared from its abstract rather than complete local full text.
Equivalent short weighted identities could remain in older unindexed Duffing literature.
title: Strict stationary RMS velocity ceiling and well-minimum crossing in the forced Duffing oscillator
